newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Aug 18.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Aug 18.

text.p: News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Media, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends

BERLIN - A Berlin court sides with Deutsche Telekom AG and prevents six private television stations from broadcasting over the company's cable system in the area of Germany's largest city. Media authorities in Berlin and the state of Brandenburg do not have the right to allow stations to broadcast on the cable network without the permission of the network owner, the court rules. Reuters)

BERLIN - Babelsberg Film Studios says film director Volker Schloendorff, whose films include Oscar-winner "The Tin Drum", is leaving his post as the studios' managing director. Schloendorff will stay on as a member the board of the studios' new holding company, but will hand over management of day-to-day activities to Friedrich-Carl Wachs on October 1. (Reuters)

LONDON - FCA! advertising agency says its recent merger with UK-based branding specialist Kelly Weedon Shute will help it grow across Europe and satisfy growing client demand for "through-the-line" service. Chris Parry, chairman and chief executive of FCA!, says his agency has enjoyed "meteoric growth" in recent years because companies are spending increasingly on direct marketing rather than more glamorous and more expensive above-the-line advertising. (Reuters)

FRANKFURT - The head of carmaker BMW AG says earnings growth in the second half of 1997 should continue at the pace of the first six months but added that the strong pound was hurting earnings at UK unit Rover. (Reuters)

FRANKFURT - Carmaker Volkswagen AG will pick up where it left off last year when it publishes 1997 first-half results that are expected to show another solid jump in profits. Industry analysts say they expect VW to report group net profit increasing to around 500 million marks ($270 million) in the first six months of the year from 282 million marks in the first half of 1996 and that sales of about 56 billion marks compared to 50 billion a year ago. (Reuters)

KONSTANZ - A German who tried to extort millions of marks from Swiss Nestle's Maggi unit by threatening to inject its food products with mad cow disease is jailed for three years and two months. (Reuters)

MUNICH - Alois Dallmayr Kaffee oHG, a German coffee roaster, says it has bought Bremen firm Azul Kaffee GmbH & Co KG retroactive to July 1, 1997. Azul, a leading provider of premium coffee products for catering, had sales of 60 million marks in 1996. (Reuters)

BERLIN - Radio reports about financial troubles at baked goods company City Back cause several hundred confused Citibank customers from Berlin and surrounding areas to rush to the branch offices and demand their savings back. Evidently, a Citibank spokesman says, the account holders had confused the name "City Back" with "Citibank". (Reuters)

FRANKFURT - Thilo Veil starts as efficient consumer response manager, a newly-created position, at haircare group Wella AG in Darmstadt. He will be responsible for expanding cooperation between Wella and retailers. (Horizont)
FRANKFURT - Cosima Reif is hired by TBWA's Berlin office as creative director, effective September 1. She was previously with Springer & Jacoby. (Frankfurt)
